loop.reading: On real python edits a wrong change is visible to the repository's own tests 0.5445 of the time and invisible 0.4555 of the time; for multi-line edits it is 0.342. The advanced edits are not where the blindness lives -- they are the best named (82.0%) -- it lives in the third of code no test names at all, plus the fifth that naming does not save.

oracle_density.definition: has_module_test: the changed module has a test file of its own name. names_a_token: the repository's whole test corpus at that commit contains an identifier taken from the lines the commit changed. Both are ceilings; naming is not asserting.

python_only.why: the strength constant (0.8021) was measured on code mutants, so the loop is computed on the python subset; the all-suffix number also counts documentation and CI configuration, which no test names

what_this_shows: Of 691 real changed sites across pallets/click, pallets/itsdangerous, pallets/markupsafe, pypa/packaging, pypa/pyproject-hooks, 0.1868 sit in a module that has a test file of its own name and 0.5042 are named somewhere in the repository's test corpus at that commit -- so the repository's own oracle can see at most that share of real work. For edits spanning two lines it is 0.6167. Multiplying by the measured strength of a passing suite (0.8021), a wrong edit is visible 0.5445 of the time and invisible 0.4555 of the time, and 0.342 for multi-line edits. This is the ceiling on the only engineerable term in P(correct) = P(determined) x P(executed) x P(seen).
